Bangladesh managed a couple of partnerships but kept losing wickets regularly. The cracks will open up more as the game progresses and it won't get any easier for the batters to score. Sri Lanka have to be careful. Can Bangladeshi bowlers manage a couple of wickets before the end of the session?

Bangladesh opted to bat first, just like they did in the first Test match but here in Colombo, they found it hard to get going as there was much more for the bowlers as compared to the first game. Sri Lankan pacers were spot on with their line and length and so were their spinners. It's surprising to see Prabath Jayasuriya without any wickets as he always delivers in home conditions. However, this time around, the debutant Sonal Dinusha took the limelight as he bowled brilliantly in his first outing.

So, Bangladesh have managed to add 27 runs to the overnight total. A fantastic bowling display from Sri Lanka and they'll be happy with how they have performed. Asitha Fernando in particular, who didn't have much to do in the first Test, used the variable bounce to a great extent as he ended with a three-fer.

Bangladesh won the toss but were pegged back by some wonderful opening spells from the two pacers, Asitha Fernando and Vishwa Fernando. However, Bangladesh recovered to end the first session at 71/2. ...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Mushfiqur Rahim fell through a reckless shot to the debutant, Sonal Dinusha. Mehidy Hasan Miraz was batting well but he edged one down to first slip which made things worse for the visitors. Nayeem Hasan was their last known lower order batter but he too fell in the final minutes of the play. Bangladesh have just two wickets in hand and Sri Lanka will be eager to turn it up and carry over the momentum. A promising start to the game. That is all from Day 1's action. The second session was a rain-affected session, that saw only 23 overs bowled. Sri Lanka tightened their grip by picking up three key wickets, leaving Bangladesh in a spot of bother at 144 for 5. Shanto and Shadman fell early, while Litton Das, despite a couple of lives, was dismissed by debutant Sonal Dinusha. Mushfiqur Rahim remained unbeaten on 34 alongside Mehidy Hasan Miraz as Bangladesh looked to rebuild in the final session.

A day that belonged to the Lankans! The first session was somewhat evenly poised as Bangladesh were 71/2. Sri Lanka’s pacers started strong and took an early wicket. Then, Bangladesh’s batters Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque played carefully and tried to settle. Mominul got out soon after, but Shadman and Najmul Hossain Shanto kept batting steadily. There were a couple of close moments, but overall, it was a balanced session.

There are still around 10 overs of play remaining but the light is not good enough to continue! Sri Lanka leave the field with noses in front. What a day for the hosts. Both teams wanted to bat first but only one have made justice to the decision. Bangladesh will feel disappointed with how they have batted. The reckless shots they have attempted which resulted only in wickets. Following the rain delay, both batters resumed with caution, denying the bowlers any openings. Litton Das, after a good knock of 34, eventually fell to debutant Sonal Dinusha, who claimed a memorable maiden test wicket. With the final session underway, the onus now lies on the experienced Mushfiqur and the lower order to guide Bangladesh to a competitive total.

Another Lankan session! Post-lunch, Bangladesh set about rebuilding their innings after a shaky morning session. Shadman Islam held his ground with commendable grit, providing much-needed stability. However, Sri Lanka's bowlers returned with some intensity and were quick to make inroads, removing both Shadman and Najmul Hossain Shanto in quick succession to get control of the match. There was a rain break for a while where the Bangladesh score was 90 for 4 in 33.2 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. Earlier, Sonal Dinusha got his maiden Test cap from Kusal Mendis. Big shoes to fill for the youngster as he comes in place of Angelo Mathews. The Lankan players are out in the middle. Shadman Islam and Anamul Haque to open for Bangladesh. Asitha Fernando to bowl first. Let's play...

Dhananjaya de Silva, the skipper of Sri Lanka says they also wanted to bat first but feels, with overcast conditions, there is something for the bowlers. Informs so comes in for Mathews and tells he will bat at 6 and DDS will bat at 4. Shares Sonal Dinusha have performed well in the last couple of years and is a good backup for Mathews.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper of Bangladesh says they will bat first as it looks a very good wicket. Informs they have made a couple of changes. Tells they did well in Galle but these are new conditions and they have to do well.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Lahiru Udara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva (C), Kusal Mendis (WK), Sonal Dinusha (In for Angelo Mathews) (On his Debut), Tharindu Rathnayake, Prabath Jayasuriya, Vishwa Fernando (In for Milan Rathnayake), Asitha Fernando.
